title: A Computationally Efficient Lumped Galerkin Method with Cubic B-Splines for Small-Amplitude Long-Wave Propagation in the Benjamin–Bona–Mahony–Burgers Equation
content: In this study, a numerical procedure is designed for solving the nonlinear Benjamin–Bona–Mahony–Burgers (BBMB) equation by combining the Strang time-splitting technique with the cubic B-spline lumped Galerkin method. The primary objective is to demonstrate that the proposed algorithm provides more accurate and efficient numerical solutions than previously reported methods. Within this framework, the original BBMB equation is decomposed into two time-dependent subproblems. Each subproblem is discretized using the cubic B-spline Galerkin finite element formulation, and the resulting systems are integrated through the Strang time-splitting procedure. The stability of the suggested numerical scheme is also investigated. To assess its performance, three benchmark problems, including cases with and without known analytical solutions, are considered. The accuracy and reliability of the method are evaluated by computing the $L_{2}$ and $L_{\infty}$ error norms together with the conservation invariants $I_1$,$I_2$ and $I_3$, corresponding to mass, energy, and momentum, respectively. The generated numerical outcomes are compared with previously documented solutions and are presented in both graphical and tabular forms. The findings indicate that the proposed method constitutes an effective and reliable computational technique for the numerical solution of nonlinear differential equations.
